translationRepairs: Shi Jilong was Shi Le's nephew, but his personal name was taboo because it matched the posthumous name of Le's grandfather
Shi Jilong was Shi Le's nephew, but his personal name was taboo because it violated the temple taboo of Taizu (of Tang)
太祖廟諱 is the Tang Taizu taboo (Li Hu), not Shi Le's grandfather.
Shi Le told their lord he meant to execute him; the lord replied, "A spirited ox will wreck wagons while still a calf—you must bear with him awhile."
Shi Le told his mother, Lady Wang, that he meant to execute him; she replied, "A spirited ox will wreck wagons while still a calf—you must bear with him awhile."
王 here is Lady Wang, Shi Le's mother.

Kui An became Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, and acting Director of the Masters of Writing; Guo Yin Minister of Works; Han Xi Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Wei Kai, Feng Mo, Zhang Chong, and Cao Xian Masters of Writing; Shen Zhong Palace Attendant; Lang Kan Supernumerary Grandee; Wang Bo Director of the Palace Secretariat; and other civil and military officers received promotions and appointments according to rank.

Kui An became Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, and acting Director of the Masters of Writing; Guo Yin Minister of Works; Han Xi Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Wei Kai, Feng Mo, Zhang Chong, and Cao Xian Masters of Writing; Shen Zhong Palace Attendant; Lang Kan Grandee of Splendid Happiness; Wang Bo Director of the Palace Secretariat; and other civil and military officers received promotions and appointments according to rank.
光祿大夫 is Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
In Xian Kang 2 (336 CE), he had Bridle Gate general Zhang Mi haul Luoyang's bell racks, Nine Dragons statues, stone guardians, bronze camels, and Feilian figures to Ye.
In Xian Kang 2 (336 CE), he had Gate General Zhang Mi haul Luoyang's bell racks, Nine Dragons statues, stone guardians, bronze camels, and Feilian figures to Ye.
Corve labor mushroomed and campaigns never ceased; drought kept grain dear—two dou of rice cost a jin of gold—and the populace howled for want of a livelihood.
Corvée labor mushroomed and campaigns never ceased; drought kept grain dear—two dou of rice cost a jin of gold—and the populace howled for want of a livelihood.
Prince Xuan of Hejian and Prince Tao of Le'an enjoyed Jilong's favor, and Shi Sui loathed them as mortal foes.
Shi Xuan, Duke of Hejian, and Shi Tao, Duke of Le'an enjoyed Jilong's favor, and Shi Sui loathed them as mortal foes.
Lady Zheng became Heavenly Queen, and Prince Shi Sui was named Heavenly Crown Prince.
Lady Zheng became Heavenly Queen, and his son Shi Sui was named Heavenly Crown Prince.
子邃 means his son Sui.

Tao Bao led a hundred-thousand-man fleet from Piaoyu Ford as General Who Spans the Sea, Wang Hua commanded as General Who Crosses the Liao, while Zhi Xiong and Yao Yizhong took a hundred thousand horse and foot as the spearhead against Duan Liao.

Tao Bao led a hundred-thousand-man fleet from Piaoyu Ford as General Who Spans the Sea, Wang Hua commanded as General Who Crosses the Liao, while Zhi Xiong, as Grand General of the Dragon Gallop, and Yao Yizhong, as General Who Leads the Army, took a hundred thousand horse and foot as the spearhead against Duan Liao.
The source gives both generals' offices.

Planning a strike on Changli, Jilong ordered Caofu Who Crosses the Liao to ferry Qingzhou troops across the sea to hold Tadun; finding no fresh water, they pulled back to offshore islets while three million hu of grain sailed out to sustain them.

Planning a strike on Changli, Jilong ordered Cao Fu, General Who Crosses the Liao to ferry Qingzhou troops across the sea to hold Tadun; finding no fresh water, they pulled back to offshore islets while three million hu of grain sailed out to sustain them.
曹伏 is the person; 渡遼 his office.
Shi Xuan took twenty thousand horse and foot against the Shuofang Xianbei chief Hushetou, shattered him, and piled up more than forty thousand heads.
Shi Xuan took twenty thousand horse and foot against the Shuofang Xianbei chief Humotou, shattered him, and piled up more than forty thousand heads.
Earlier Princes Shegui and Rigui had garrisoned Chang'an; both memorialized that western commander Shi Guang was currying favor and plotting sedition.
Earlier Shegui, Duke of Xiangcheng, and Rigui, Duke of Shangyong, had garrisoned Chang'an; both memorialized that western commander Shi Guang was currying favor and plotting sedition.
Supervisor Wang Bo urged: "Li Hong vows to serve faithfully—should he regain Shu he will gather his clan and submit to civilization.
Supervisor of the Secretariat Wang Bo urged: "Li Hong vows to serve faithfully—should he regain Shu he will gather his clan and submit to civilization.
中書監 is Supervisor of the Secretariat.
Shi Min broke the Jin army south of the Han; General Cai Huai fell in the fight.
Shi Min broke the Jin army at Mianyin; General Cai Huai fell in the fight.
沔陰 is south of the Mian river.

Personnel chief Liu Zhen protested that this betrayed merit assessment; Jilong punished the clerks who had distorted policy and promoted Liu Zhen to Superior Grand Master with gold seal and purple sash.

光祿大夫 is Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
Wary of Shi Hu's power, Zhang Jun dispatched Administrator Ma Shen to pay homage.
Wary of Shi Hu's power, Zhang Jun dispatched his Attendant Officer Ma Shen to pay homage.
別駕 is the Attendant Officer, not an administrator.
Even Han Mingdi stopped palace work on one minister's word.
Emperor Ming of Han, a worthy ruler, stopped the Deyang palace work on one word from Zhongli.
The source names Zhongli and Deyang.
I am no Zhongli Yan, yet you surpass the Han emperors—please listen."
My insight shames the worthies of old such as Zhongli, yet you surpass the Han emperors—please listen."
昔士 alludes to Zhongli Yi; Yan was an error.
Zhang Li, commanding the Ministry of Five Armies, flattered Shi Xuan: "Princely armies exceed statute—pare them back to magnify the throne."
Right Supervisor Zhang Li, concurrently Minister of the Five Armies, flattered Shi Xuan: "Princely armies exceed statute—pare them back to magnify the throne."
右僕射 and 領五兵尚書.
Power flowed through Shen Bian—most governors flattered him while a dozen high ministers alone stood on ceremony.
Power flowed through Shen Bian—most governors flattered him while only Palace Attendants Zheng Xi and Wang Mo, Regular Attendants Lu Chen and Cui Yue, and some ten others treated him as an equal.
The source names the officials who resisted.
"Shen Zhong warned that rewards, punishments, and offices belong to the sovereign alone.
"Minister of Education Shen Zhong warned that rewards, punishments, and offices belong to the sovereign alone.
The source gives his office 司徒.
Zhou and Zheng fell to rival sons—unchecked favor destroys bloodlines, Majesty."
Zhou suffered the rising of Prince Tui and Zheng the revolt of Shu Duan—unchecked favor destroys bloodlines, Majesty."
The source names 子頹 and 叔段.
Prince Shi Jian, son of Shi Hu, was then garrisoning Guanzhong, where repeated labor levies and heavy taxes alienated the people west of the passes.
Shi Jian, Duke of Yiyang,, son of Shi Hu, was then garrisoning Guanzhong, where repeated labor levies and heavy taxes alienated the people west of the passes.
義陽公 is Duke of Yiyang.

The chief clerk exposed the scheme; Shi Hu sent Right Supervisor Zhang Li west as Left Chief Clerk of the West, Dragon-Gallop General and Inspector of Yongzhou to investigate, recalled Shi Jian, jailed Li Song, and installed Shi Bao at Chang'an.
When floods stalled the roads, eunuch Yan Sheng accused Minister Zhu Gui of sabotage and slander; Shi Hu executed Gui.
When floods stalled the roads, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yan Sheng accused Minister Zhu Gui of sabotage and slander; Shi Hu executed Gui.
中黃門 is Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
